sections.heading: Quick review

lines.en: I drink tea.
Sometimes I work at home.
What's your name? Said to a woman.

sections.note: Say each phrase aloud before you hear the English.

sections.heading: Dialogue

lines.en: Where is Ahmad today?
He's working at home today.

lines.ar: وَفَاطِمَةُ؟ هَلْ تَعْمَلُ فِي الْبَيْتِ أَيْضًا؟
lines.en: And Fatima? Is she working at home too?

lines.ar: لَا، هِيَ فِي الْمَكْتَبِ. تَرْسُمُ تَصْمِيمًا جَدِيدًا.
lines.en: No, she's at the office. She's drawing a new design.
Does she drink coffee?
Yes, she drinks coffee every morning.
And what does Ahmad do in the morning?
He drinks tea, then he writes programs.
The team is excellent!
Thanks, praise be to Allah.

sections.note: Listen, then read it aloud. Play both roles. A friend asks Ridhwan about his team's day.

sections.heading: How it works

lines.en: he writes
she writes, or you write, to a man
He works at home.
She drinks coffee.

sections.note: For he, the present tense starts with ya: yaktubu, he writes. For she, it starts with ta: taktubu, she writes. That is the same form as you, to a man, so context tells you which one is meant.

sections.heading: Word builder: the root raa, seen, meem, meaning drawing

lines.en: he drew
a drawing
an artist, one who draws as a job
a studio, the place of drawing

sections.note: You know maf-al, the place. Today's new pattern is fa-aal, with a doubled middle letter: someone who does the action as a job or a lot. Rassaam is an artist. Compare faa-il, which is simply the doer.

sections.heading: Speak it

lines.en: What does your colleague do in the morning?
Model answer: My colleague drinks coffee, then he works.
Where does your female colleague work?

lines.ar: زَمِيلَتِي تَعْمَلُ فِي الْمَكْتَبِ فِي لَاغُوسَ.
lines.en: Model answer: My colleague works at the office in Lagos.
Does your brother study?
Model answer: Yes, my brother studies in Lagos.

sections.note: Answer each question aloud about yourself. Then listen to the model answer.
